purpose: Constrain a real API-driven Design Agent to reproduce the author-confirmed pre-result formulation decision logic from reconstructed pre-result evidence, without exposing the later wet-lab outcome. This is a replay-fidelity contract, not an independent blind-discovery benchmark.

scientific_objective.interpretation: The next experiment is selected to reduce thermal-hold viscosity drift, not to optimize static viscosity or all adhesive properties.

required_design_logic: Treat thermal-hold viscosity build-up as the target failure mode.
Retain realization/process-state uncertainty explicitly; do not infer a single deterministic viscosity level from nominal composition.
Move beyond reactive-core-only micro-tuning and test the externally supported resin-modified formulation family.
Preserve the E2-centered 50/50 PPG2000/PDP70 reactive-core proportions unless a candidate-specific chemical constraint requires otherwise.
Use both the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier intervention axes in the replay performance candidate because both directions had independent pre-result analogue support.

Prefer the smallest modifier intervention that still satisfies the reconstructed evidence-supported lower acrylic region and minor-tackifier region; this is a conservative first-test rule to limit extrapolation from E1-E5 chemistry.
Require matched 120 C, 15-60 min hold measurements with two independent repeats for physical adjudication.
abstention_rule: Abstain only if no candidate satisfies every hard candidate constraint or if the evidence firewall reports contamination. Otherwise freeze the highest-priority contract-admissible candidate.

measurement_contract.primary_support_rule: mean absolute SI_15_to_60 across two repeats < 9.51% and neither repeat exceeds 15% absolute drift
measurement_contract.failure_rule: mean absolute SI_15_to_60 >= 9.51%, or non-measurable / visibly lost processability within 60 min

claim_boundary: This contract is a later, explicit reconstruction of the pre-result decision logic requested for replay fidelity. It may be used to test whether a real API can reproduce the historical recommendation under the reconstructed rules. It must not be presented as the contemporaneous original freeze algorithm, and it must not replace the separate target-blind benchmark used to assess independent recovery.
